proposed.text: An architect's plan shows a Basic R-2 lot (no firewall) where the building footprint is 55%, paved driveways occupy 35%, and planted area is 10%. Per Table VIII.1, is this layout compliant?

options.text: Compliant — PSO (55%) meets the maximum, and TOSL (45%) meets the minimum open space requirement
Non-compliant — the ISA (35%) exceeds the 30% maximum ISA for Basic R-2 without firewall per Table VIII.1
Non-compliant — the USA (10%) is below the 15% minimum USA for Basic R-2 without firewall per Table VIII.1
Non-compliant on two counts: ISA exceeds 30% maximum AND USA is below 15% minimum per Table VIII.1

proposed.rationale: Original question was already source-correct and substantive; the prior edit (source-audited-article-batch-048) was degenerate, with 1-character garbage in 3 of 4 option text fields and a nonsensical rationale. Restored the original verbatim. Original source rationale: Table VIII.1 for Basic R-2 without firewall: max PSO=55%, max ISA=30%, min USA=15%. This layout has ISA=35% (exceeds 30% max) AND USA=10% (below 15% min). Both ISA and USA independently violate their respective limits. PSO compliance alone (55%) is not sufficient. Option A ignores the ISA cap and USA floor. Option B or C each catch only one violation.
proposed.explanation: Three independently enforced limits exist: max PSO, max ISA, and min USA. Meeting one or two does not ensure compliance. Basic R-2 without firewall: PSO max 55%, ISA max 30%, USA min 15%. With ISA=35% and USA=10%, both ISA and USA fail. The MACA check (55+35=90%) also exceeds 85%, confirming the dual failure.
